sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
GRE Renew Enertech Limited is a small solar engineering, procurement and construction contractor building an owned renewable-power portfolio, with a shrinking legacy LED/overseas retail component. Revenue growth and commissioned assets are genuine strengths: consolidated revenue grew at 33.0% over FY23–FY26 and solar activities grew faster. The investment case is an execution-led EPC/RESCO growth thesis, not yet an evidence-backed compounder. At the dated ₹245 close, current issued shares imply ₹350.056 crore equity value and 25.78 times reported FY26 profit.

The decisive problem is evidence quality, not merely valuation. Consolidation audit-scope wording and IPO-cost/object disclosures conflict; current funding after commissioning is not verified; and incremental project returns cannot be attributed to the capital invested. BQS, GQS (Growth Quality Score) and IAS therefore remain NS. G2 and G3 are holds, not proven fraud or default. A base operating diagnostic produces 13.28% hypothetical five-year return after assumed transaction friction, but ordinary investor return and entry-price fields remain null. Reopen only after accounting/proceeds reconciliation, current funding verification, plant-level economics and adequate BSE execution evidence.

sections.text:
Legal identity: GRE Renew Enertech Limited, formerly GRE Renew Enertech Private Limited and earlier GRE Electronics Private Limited. BSE SME scrip 544682, symbol GRERENEW, ISIN INE0U8P01015. Partnership roots date to 1999; the corporate entity was incorporated in 2008 and listed on 21 January 2026. Do not substitute similarly named renewable companies. The official interoperable security master identifies a BSE-eligible SM line, not an NSE listing.

Research cutoff is 20 October 2026, India information basis; retrieval occurred 21 October with no later operating information used. The latest appropriate dated secondary close is ₹245 on 19 October, ahead of the 20 October exchange holiday. Shares are 14,288,000; market capitalization is ₹350.056 crore. Scope is consolidated Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards, not assumed Ind AS. FY21–FY22 parent-only background is deliberately separated. Horizon is five calendar years to 19 October 2031, nominal INR, before personal taxes; hurdle 15%, sensitivities 12% and 18%. The illustrative ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is not a recommended position.

G1 is Conditional: specific reporting/related-party concerns but no evidenced severe integrity failure. G2 is Hold: material contradictory audit and IPO disclosures need resolution. G3 is Hold: current cash, bank availability and remaining project obligations are not verified despite low dated debt and favorable rating commentary. G4 is Conditional, not failed: real trading and the lot are established, complete current execution conditions are not. Confidence is High on legal identity and dated lot/share count, Medium on reported financial transcription/business history, Low on accounting clarification, incremental returns, current funding and executable liquidity. Overall conclusion confidence is Low.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The thirteen canonical factors are assigned once and reused without extra bonuses: GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 4, BAL 5, EXEC 6, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P 4 and L NS. Every factor has multiple factual supports, contrary evidence, source references, confidence and an explicit scoring anchor in the embedded audit. REV starts at 9 for the chosen three-year reported CAGR, but the four-observation/Medium-confidence ceiling reduces it to 8; no trajectory adjustment is added.

BQS known weighted contribution is 4.44 with 88% coverage; the missing-CAP mathematical range is 4.56–5.64. GQS known contribution is 5.55 with 85% coverage; its range is 5.70–7.05. IAS known contribution is 1.00 with 30% coverage; missing Q, R and L make its range 1.70–8.00. These are bounds under unknown scores of 1–10, not confidence intervals, estimates or rankable points. All raw/final composites remain null/NS.

No numeric override is applied: no G1 failure, no evidenced G3 failure, and no persistent CAP or CASH score of 3 or below. G2 prevents numerical ranking independently of missing CAP. G3 alone would not mechanically exclude a complete, reliable quality score. Moving uncertain MOAT and DUR one point together shifts the known BQS contribution by 0.30 and GQS by 0.20; this illustrates judgment noise rather than curing missing evidence. Decimal weights, contribution strings and bound arithmetic are reproducible. No hidden overall score or post-hoc risk haircut is used.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The dominant business is turnkey solar EPC: design, engineering, procurement, civil/electrical construction, installation, testing and commissioning for industrial, commercial and institutional buyers. Customers generally own CAPEX-model assets; their entire cumulative installed capacity does not belong to GRE. FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹122.9216 crore: solar EPC ₹111.7896 crore, power sales ₹2.3160 crore and other business ₹8.8160 crore. EPC therefore contributes roughly 91%, whereas power is still below 2%. LED sales and the wholly owned D K USA business make the group less than a pure-play power producer.

RESCO economics differ: GRE owns plants, invests upfront, operates them and collects tariff revenue under PPAs. The June presentation described 25-year government rooftop contracts around ₹5.04/kWh and ground-mounted tariffs around ₹4/kWh. The ₹15.525 MW DC portfolio figure combines existing and newly commissioned owned assets and is distinct from more than 100 MW cumulative third-party EPC execution. Annual revenue per installed MW depends on commissioning date, yield, curtailment, tariff, collections and ownership, not nameplate capacity alone.

At March, subsidiaries were D K USA and GRE Green Energy; subsequent wholly owned Solarsource and Solarcatch project companies and nonprofit GRE Foundation increase organizational complexity without creating outside cash. Their internal EPC, equity and loan transactions must eliminate on consolidation. New authorizations are ceilings, not binding external orders, revenue or funded capital.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
GRE has operating history, local project execution experience, customer/vendor relationships and practical engineering capability. Government-site rooftop installations and larger ground projects establish a degree of qualification and delivery credibility. These can reduce customer search and execution risk. Yet the records do not demonstrate a durable proprietary technology, dominant market share, unusually low lifecycle cost, persistent pricing premium or structurally superior collection terms. Solar procurement and EPC bidding are competitive, and client concentration can transfer economic value to the buyer rather than the contractor.

Three relevant primary-source comparators provide boundaries, not a borrowed valuation: Waaree Renewable Technologies demonstrates much larger-scale solar EPC capability; KPI Green Energy combines power ownership and CPP/IPP development; Solarium is an overlapping EPC participant and GRE's particularly important customer. Their scale, integration, financing, capacity mix and market liquidity differ. This review has not produced matched-cutoff peer financial multiples, so none is represented as GRE fair value. It also does not claim one is inferior merely because its share price or reported margin differs.

Long PPAs improve duration of owned-asset cash flow, but project ownership alone is not a moat if entry capital earns ordinary returns. The appropriate MOAT score is 4 until repeat profitable customer wins, full lifecycle returns and competitive cost/qualification advantages are independently supported. Industry growth and backlog belong in DUR/REV rather than an extra moat bonus.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Consolidated revenue observations are ₹52.2190 crore in FY23, ₹90.3401 crore in FY24, ₹83.7173 crore in FY25 and ₹122.9216 crore in FY26. Actual annual additions were ₹38.1211 crore, minus ₹6.6228 crore and ₹39.2043 crore. The selected three-year CAGR is 33.02498%; the intervening decline is not omitted. The latest annual rise is 46.83%, not evidence that every project will repeat. Four group observations cannot produce a five-year CAGR, and the earlier standalone parent revenue of ₹20.311655/₹11.373970 crore in FY21/FY22 must not be stitched into group growth.

The economic cross-check is solar EPC plus power: ₹29.3030, ₹72.4165, ₹77.1609 and ₹114.1056 crore over FY23–FY26, or 57.3252% CAGR. FY26's group revenue addition breaks into EPC ₹35.0363 crore, power ₹1.9084 crore and other ₹2.2596 crore. This supports real solar expansion even as US retail activity, asset disposals and legacy LEDs complicate group organic-volume interpretation. Module-price pass-through and recognized project milestones are not separated from physical demand, so this is not labeled a verified volume CAGR.

Prospectus customer tables report 62.42% FY25 and 78.78% H1FY26 top-ten concentration on their stated operating-business denominator; the table totals indicate the domestic base, so these percentages are not silently relabeled group concentration. H1FY26 group revenue was ₹43.8044 crore; it is not annualized into a FY27 forecast. No FY27 interim result was verified before cutoff.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The runway has two different capital needs. Third-party EPC grows with execution personnel, procurement, guarantees, working capital and client advances. Owned RESCO plants require upfront capex, land/grid arrangements, commissioning, maintenance and customer payment performance. The May commissioning filings support tangible progress: IPO projects began generating on 27 May and the subsidiary's Indrap plant on 30 May. The IPO originally described 9.99 MW DC, while the generation notice states 9.67 MW DC; the presentation gives 9.6768 MW. The AC capacity stays 7.20 MW. This is a disclosed capacity difference to reconcile, not an invented plant expansion.

The annual model explicitly links EPC growth, generating MW, tariff/yield, margins, working capital, capex and financing. Base effective owned DC capacity moves from 12.0 MW in FY27 to 24.525 MW in FY32, with 1,550 kWh/kW annual yield and ₹4.30/kWh blended tariff. These are assumptions anchored to disclosed plants and tariff ranges, not management guidance or verified plant yield. Additional owned capacity costs approximately ₹4 crore/MW DC in later model years, plus maintenance/other capex; those are sensitivity inputs, not engineering quotations.

Dated operating capital rose from ₹19.7761 crore to ₹44.6678 crore. A one-year delta-NOPAT/delta-IC proxy of 18.81% is positive but mixes multiple projects, working capital, timing and translated foreign balances. No attributable project return is established, so CAP remains NS. A 12–18% nominal discount sensitivity is analytical, not a measured WACC. Attractive growth quality cannot be concluded from reported ROCE or tariff duration without full costs and cash realization.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter experience and the 69.99% promoter-group stake at IPO align a substantial part of economic ownership, but neither fact proves minority protection. The three director remuneration amounts total ₹0.45 crore in FY26, roughly 3.3% of group reported PAT, which is not obviously excessive. More material are ₹6.9613 crore of external loans/receivables involving related overseas persons/entities, whose commercial terms, ageing and recoverability require verification. Internal subsidiary loans are eliminated in group analysis and are not confused with these external receivables.

The August auditor departure must be described fairly. The resignation letter identifies failure to agree a fee revision after listing and explicitly denies non-cooperation, missing information, management scope restrictions, accounting disagreement or other material reasons. A new auditor was proposed/appointed to fill the vacancy subject to shareholder process. This is not evidence of auditor whistleblowing. The CFO departure and expanded subsidiary structure are transition items requiring continuity checks, not proof of wrongdoing.

Governance concern instead arises from actual disclosures: the audit report says subsidiary accounts were audited by other auditors while the policy describes them as unaudited; connected-loan confirmations are incomplete; share-premium issue costs differ from object-utilization costs. The old FY22 notes also admitted incomplete information on transactions with struck-off companies. The current unmodified opinion is contrary evidence, not a complete answer. New intra-group EPC approval limits as high as ₹500 crore per entity are authorizations, not external orders or funded expansion. G1 is Conditional with GOV 4, not a severe integrity failure.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Financial history and calculation bridges are embedded, with units and scope. FY23–FY26 group PAT is ₹0.8927/₹9.9052/₹7.0264/₹13.5774 crore; CFO is minus ₹2.8680/₹5.8102/₹10.6551/₹4.5572 crore. Four-year reported conversion is 0.5781x, or 0.5732x using the FY26 annual's different FY25 comparator. This is explicitly a mixed-presentation diagnostic: prospectus restatement changed tax/gratuity and cash-flow presentation. Four-year cash capex totals ₹24.2260 crore and FCF proxy minus ₹6.0715 crore. Interest is financing in reported CFO and must be deducted separately for owner cash, not twice.

FY26's CFO bridge begins with ₹18.0937 crore PBT, adds D&A/finance and removes stated interest income to get ₹18.5671 crore before working capital. Inventory absorbs ₹7.3206 crore and loans/advances ₹14.2144 crore; payables and other current liabilities supply ₹5.3468/₹4.1249 crore. Taxes and other movements yield reported CFO ₹4.5572 crore. Broad advances include supplier, tax and financial balances; translation and provision classifications still need reconciliation. Capex does not explain weak CFO. Trade receivable days improved to 27.88 from 31.46 using average balances/total revenue, but balances older than one year increased to ₹2.1737 crore from ₹0.8556 crore. Inventory-days proxy increased to 34.42 from 25.96. A falsely precise mixed-denominator cash-conversion cycle is not shown.

Reported PAT contains ₹1.24 crore liquidated damages and ₹1.0281 crore translation income. Excluding all ₹2.8613 crore other income gives operating EBITDA ₹16.1453 crore and EBIT ₹15.4284 crore; a 26% tax proxy gives normalized PAT ₹11.2720 crore. This conservative bridge also excludes some recurring commissions. The rating's ₹14.57 crore PAT numerically equals PBT less current tax before the ₹0.9931 crore deferred-tax charge; it is not substituted for audited ₹13.5774 crore.

The cash bridge reconciles to ₹30.7858 crore within rounding. IPO net issuance cash ₹34.8512 crore is already included. Equity charges ₹4.7128 crore issue costs while the utilization certificate says ₹4.0036 crore; the ₹0.7092 crore difference is not explained by an invented prepaid/GST addback. Revised allocations total ₹35.5604 crore although the narrative repeats ₹35.2281 crore net proceeds. These inconsistencies, and audited/unaudited subsidiary wording, sustain G2 Hold without labeling the audit formally qualified.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹245 and 1.4288 crore current issued shares, market value is ₹350.056 crore. Current-share reported P/E is 25.78x; dividing by historical weighted-average EPS ₹12.08 gives 20.28x and understates the claim base after the IPO. Dated book multiple is 4.40x. October market value plus March debt less March non-FD cash produces a diagnostic EV of ₹322.7656 crore, not a verified current EV. Operating property, land, transmission assets, CWIP and project inventory are valued through operating cash flow/EV and never added again. Related financial loans and FDs receive no extra terminal recovery credit.

The linked model has six fiscal rows FY27–FY32 and interpolates the exact 19 October 2031 terminal, five calendar years after entry. Bear/base/bull EPC margins are 8%/11.5%/14%, terminal EV/EBITDA 8x/12x/16x, with distinct growth, power output, collection and capex paths. Cash tax is 26%; existing principal, old tax payable and hypothetical new shares/cash are explicit. No dividends are assumed. Base/bull model balances happen to remain positive, but actual October balances, remaining project cash calls and available bank facilities are unverified. Therefore all ordinary investor IRRs and hurdle entry prices are null.

Non-investable terminal algebra gives ₹85.42/₹475.76/₹1,112.14 for bear/base/bull after retaining ₹2 crore operating cash, not adding all terminal cash as excess. The unfunded bear has no diagnostic IRR or hurdle entry. Mathematically funded base/bull diagnostics are 13.28%/34.25% after friction, not verified-current funded returns or recommendations. Bear requires ₹11.33 crore to preserve a ₹2 crore buffer through the terminal; hypothetical equity rescue at ₹147 with 5% issue cost is separately modeled and dilutes shareholders. Nine linked growth/multiple sensitivities, seven cash/timing stresses, nine DCF discount/terminal-growth sensitivities and 12%/15%/18% reverse expectations are fully embedded. Funding is tested through 19 October 2031; full FY32 deficits are separate. A late-FY32 capex sensitivity verifies that a deficit after exit does not retroactively invalidate the modeled pre-exit path, subject to unknown intra-year timing. DCF and reverse expectations retain the same operating-cash floor. DCF is a dated operating cross-check, not an investable price. No probability-weighted average IRR is presented.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case begins with a large EPC customer or procurement disruption: execution slows, customer advances do not repeat, supplier commitments remain, cash margins fall and collections age. The company's 50 MW AC Solarium award is ₹170 crore EPC plus ₹5 crore O&M; this concentration can dominate a company whose previous annual EPC revenue was ₹111.8 crore. Backlog is neither profit nor cash, and it is not automatically non-cancellable. The earlier Mehsana Dairy withdrawal already demonstrates that an EPC receivable can turn into a partially built project held for resale rather than cash.

The linked bear model lowers EPC revenue initially, margins to 8%, yield/tariff and collections while retaining project spending. It produces an ₹11.33 crore gap to a ₹2 crore buffer through the terminal before rescue. A separate combined slow-collection/full-commitment stress is harsher. Terminal cash improvement cannot cure an earlier payment default; no loan draw is assumed simply because a rating covers a proposed facility. A discounted equity rescue changes both cash and per-share ownership, not just the balance sheet.

The decisive thesis-break variable is conversion of recognized solar work and new power output into freely available cash after remaining capital obligations. Warning evidence includes continued ageing, further unexplained connected balances, or delayed certified generation. Permanent loss could also arise from accounting corrections or loss of order economics. Low dated debt, unmodified opinion and existing operating plants are meaningful contrary facts. Liquidation values, pledge priorities and actual realization of related loans are not verified, so book assets are not a downside floor.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold share-price outcome over five years requires 37.97% annual price growth; tenfold requires 58.49%. Over ten years the corresponding requirements are 17.46% and 25.89%. These are mathematical hurdles, not targets. At the current ₹350.056 crore market capitalization and no dilution, 5×/10× would require ₹1,750.28/₹3,500.56 crore equity values. At a normalized 20x owner P/E, required PAT is ₹87.514/₹175.028 crore; at a 10% owner net margin that means ₹875.14/₹1,750.28 crore revenue, about 7.1×/14.2× FY26 revenue. Lower terminal multiples or dilution raise those operating requirements.

The base diagnostic does not deliver fivefold over five years. The bull includes much faster EPC expansion and more owned generation, yet it remains dependent on funding, margins, collection discipline and exit valuation that are not verified. Owned generation is capital-intensive, while EPC scaling must keep guarantees and working capital proportional to real cash economics. Merely adding internal subsidiary authorization ceilings cannot support the required revenue or financing.

The correct designation is Speculative / unsupported for 5× or 10× as an investment thesis today. A long solar demand runway and a small starting equity value make such outcomes mathematically possible, but neither establishes attributable reinvestment returns or minority per-share compounding. No success probability, promised multibagger target or allocation is inferred.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
First resolve the accounting gate: obtain a signed reconciliation of subsidiary audit status, IPO issue costs, actual net proceeds, prepaid amounts and revised object allocations. The baseline differences are ₹0.7092 crore issue cost and ₹0.3323 crore revised allocation arithmetic. Unexplained persistence is a hold; an adverse correction or substantiated diversion would require a fresh integrity assessment, not automatic reliance on this score.

Track current unrestricted/earmarked cash, FDs, used and unused sanctioned bank facilities, drawing power, expiry, repayment and project-payable schedules. Compare verified available funding with linked model gaps, not the ₹35 crore rated amount or intra-group authorization ceilings. Obtain actual FY27 interim results and cash flow before updating R. Track external related loans at ₹6.9613 crore, supplier advances ₹11.5973 crore, receivables older than one year ₹2.1737 crore and debtor-day/ageing divergence. Deterioration without collections or a documented project bridge warrants investigation.

Verify final GEDA commissioning certificates, metered generation, realized tariffs, curtailment and plant operating costs for IPO/Indrap projects. Compare achieved output with the base 1,550 kWh/kW assumption and reconcile original 9.99 MW DC to commissioned 9.67 MW. Track the Solarium contract's approved milestones, cash advances, recognized margins and cancellations; do not re-add its value to total backlog. Review new auditor/CFO continuity and external versus internal subsidiary sales. Before any execution, obtain complete BSE 60-session actual values, current surveillance/restrictions, lot and live spread/depth. The ₹5 lakh reference must be replaced with an actual intended position if supplied. These are research checks, not scheduled automations or trading instructions.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: Hold — unresolved; execution-led EPC/RESCO growth research watchlist, not an evidence-backed compounder or an eligible attractive-entry conclusion. BQS and GQS remain NS because CAP cannot be established; IAS also lacks R and L. G2 prevents ranking while material accounting clarification is pending. G3's current funding hold is separately tracked and does not itself establish distress or erase the historical business's strengths. No governance cap is applied, and this is not an Avoid — governance verdict.

Research priority is meaningful because solar revenue expansion, delivered assets and low dated debt deserve investigation. The next useful work is not a price target: it is reconciliation of financial/proceeds evidence, current committed funding, attributable project cash returns and tradability. A completed, reliable factor set would then be rescored under the unchanged framework. A cheaper market quotation may improve valuation assumptions but cannot answer those missing questions.

For an existing holder, the record identifies reliability, funding, cash conversion, customer concentration and exit-liquidity questions. It is not a personalized sell instruction because holdings, portfolio exposure, taxes, alternative uses and actual execution conditions have not been supplied. For a new purchase, no ordinary hurdle entry is offered while the gates remain unresolved. One BSE lot at the reference quote is ₹2.94 lakh, while two cost ₹5.88 lakh and exceed the illustrative ₹5 lakh reference. Neither is represented as suitable for the user.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source hierarchy begins with the issuer's final prospectus, audited annual report, proceeds certificate, commissioning notices, project settlement and auditor letter. The rating is an independent credit opinion, not an audit or a cash-facility sanction; management presentations and order announcements are labeled as claims. Official exchange master/codebook establish identity, dated shares and lot. Secondary dated OHLCV is used only because the public BSE bhavcopy request returned an access-error document rather than data. Unknown observations are retained as missing. Primary peer pages support qualitative capability comparisons, not matched valuation multiples.

All material claims map to evidence/source IDs and page or section locators. Local source-byte SHA256 hashes are preserved when a document was downloaded; web-only reads and failed downloads are explicitly labeled. The final report, financial extracts, model inputs, annual outputs, sensitivity rows and source URLs are self-contained. Raw issuer PDFs, OCR text, screenshots and shareholder documents are excluded from private Library packages because they may contain unnecessary personal identifiers. Those omissions limit independent re-reading, not the local calculation audit. Reacquire omitted material from its exact source URL and compare the recorded hash before verification.

Open questions are current cash/funding, subsidiary audit scope, foreign related-loan recovery, IPO cost/prepaid/GST reconciliation, supplier-advance allocation between projects and operations, current project obligations, plant-level returns, backlog cancellation/collections, later shareholding/encumbrance changes and full BSE execution data. No missing value is silently zero. Gross profit, complete credit-sales/purchase-based CCC, five-year comparable group CAGR, legal-entity tax schedules and mature cohort returns remain ND or NS as appropriate. No raw taxpayer identifier, broker action, outside communication or recurring monitor is part of this deliverable.
